Counts20-byte collision-source entries starting at resource+64 whose type byte+4 equals the requested type. Limitations: Header count and loaded resource extent are prerequisites; malformed resources are outside the native routine's safety contract.

Iterates source entries selected by a bitmask over their type byte, rather than treating17 as a literal type number. Limitations: Mask17 selects bits0/4; names for those categories have not been established.

Converts a source entry into a40-byte shape: type+0, radius+4, height+8, source pointer+16 and transformed center Vec4+24; bone/pose gating can zero dimensions. Limitations: These are collision proxies, not an asserted final damage hitbox layout for every actor.

Initializes the Actor world block at+1744, invalid floor state at+1860, polygonFFFF, null dynamic owner; loads collision resource+2744 and allocates body+2560/hurt+1600 buffers. Limitations: A constructor state with flags2 must not be interpreted as grounded. Static claim covers these initialization paths only.
Releases both Actor body/hurt shape collections during cleanup. Limitations: No general generation counter or post-free pointer clearing was identified here.

Performs Actor cleanup including shape-buffer release and Actor allocation release. Limitations: A retained Actor pointer can remain readable after this function; live-list/status ownership is required.

Rebinds a collision resource, updates world dimensions and creates new body/hurt buffers without first releasing the old buffers in this body. Limitations: No direct runtime caller was found in the examined index. Do not repurpose as a trainer refresh API.

Runs body-to-body separation via3BA970/40AD70 independently of the world-collision gate and resolver; copies the refreshed support-cache result flags. Limitations: This distinguishes the proposed body-only bit from the existing complete movement-collision bypass.

Returns cached floor Y when valid; on an invalid cache it invokes3F3DD0 and writes the Actor cache, possibly clearing the invalid-height bit. Limitations: Not a side-effect-free getter; the trainer reads the guarded cache directly.

Returns an action-dependent Actor+256 value for selected descriptors, otherwise shares the mutating floor-cache refresh behavior. Limitations: Not a universal current-ground getter and not called by diagnostics.

Writes start/displacement into the live Actor collision block and runs the resolver before returning a result bit. Limitations: Cannot be used as a harmless 'can move there' test; it changes the live block and shared filters.

Probes the ground under an Actor and uses the position-setting path when a hit is accepted. Limitations: Potential snap-to-floor API needs separate caller, action and transition validation; no trainer call is implemented.

Sets Actor+1876 dynamic-platform/snap tolerance from the decoded platform-parent context and a native constant. Limitations: The tolerance is context-owned and not exposed as a persistent trainer override.

Pops a24-byte node from the dynamic-collider pool, constructs its248-byte collider and links the node into the global list. Limitations: The native allocator assumes available pool capacity; it is not a checked mod allocation API.
Unlinks a dynamic collider node, releases its collider pointer+8 and returns its index to the free stack. Limitations: Requires a known current linked node. Never pass a cached or guessed node.
Iterates dynamic nodes while skipping flag2-disabled nodes. Limitations: Packed next links and list lifetime still require independent validation.

Creates map collision wrappers of248 bytes and binds the loaded map collision/environment resources, including static rootABD448. Limitations: Wrappers are scene-owned; their existence is not permanent process lifetime.
Releases and nulls the map collider wrapper globals and associated map root during teardown. Limitations: Snapshots require a current playable scene and fresh root validation.

Binds a248-byte collider wrapper to resource tables: polygon+24, vertex+32, attribute+40, normal+48, counts+72..84, matrices+100/+164 and scratch flags. Limitations: Raw header offsets/counts are trusted by native code; this is not a safe arbitrary external-mesh parser.

Dispatches shape intersection: type1 cylinders, type3 spheres, and supported type0 ellipsoid combinations, with strict overlap comparisons. Limitations: Unsupported type combinations return false; tangency is not overlap and zero dimensions can divide by zero.

Derives horizontal separation for supported type0/3 pairs with a native skin allowance of5. Limitations: Does not resolve arbitrary shapes or vertical penetration; unsupported pairs leave correction unchanged.
Updates pose/transforms and rebuilds the body-shape buffer+2560 through40B140. Limitations: Body shape data follows pose lifetime and may be computed on the native motion workers.
Performs Actor motion work and rebuilds the hurt-shape buffer+1600 after body/pose processing. Limitations: This worker entry must finish before an external observer assumes stable shape data.

Queues batches of Actor motion jobs via12FDB0 and waits via130130 before returning; then clears the active work flag. Limitations: Trainer snapshot placement after the original native update relies on this normal completion path, not arbitrary worker sampling.
Runs the Actor update phase including3BFD30 and invokes the motion/pose batch processing before post-update processing. Limitations: A frame may still skip collision for native stop/action states.

Registers the field Actor-update task and its cleanup and creates the subordinate Actor scheduler with the3BF5E0 callback. Limitations: Task/scene lifetime is required; merely finding an Actor address is insufficient.
Iterates collision-source entries and skips entries whose group is disabled by3BA550. Limitations: Native enabled-shape count can vary with action and group masks within one Actor lifetime.
Implements the supported mixed ellipsoid/cylinder overlap calculation using radial cross sections. Limitations: No broad physics-engine interpretation beyond the examined proxy pair is claimed.
Tests normalized ellipsoid-style squared separation against1 for supported shape pairs. Limitations: Nonzero dimensions are required; the routine is unsuitable for arbitrary malformed input.

Builds shape bounds but uses MINSS for subsequent upper bounds as well as lower bounds; full ASM confirms upper X/Y/Z can shrink. Limitations: This is a literal static anomaly. Visible gameplay impact is not proven; the normal model-bounds path differs.

Allocates2248 bytes for the dynamic-node pool, initializes80 nodes/free indices and clears dynamic list head/tail. Limitations: 80 is the pool allocator capacity, not proof that every possible list node must belong to this pool.
Clears numeric flag1 on a dynamic node. Limitations: This is a lateral-pass flag operation, not node destruction.

Constructs/appends a dynamic node provided by the caller instead of allocating it from the80-node pool. Limitations: No direct code caller was found in the inspected index. External-node reachability remains unproven.

Ground probe receives startRCX, outputRDX, rangeXMM2, biasXMM3 and a stack mask; writes a fallback output on failure and returns a hit boolean. Limitations: Calls shared collider-query machinery and is not used by trainer readouts.

Fetches a plane normal through the polygon's normal index, transforms and normalizes it for a nonidentity collider. Limitations: Requires valid polygon/normal indices and loaded tables; trainer copies the native cache instead of following these tables.
Allocates through the current scene heap's virtual allocation slot. Limitations: Shape collections belong to scene heap9BA920; no cross-scene ownership is implied.
Releases through the current scene heap's virtual release slot. Limitations: Calling it after heap replacement with an old allocation is unsafe.
Clears Actor+288 numeric mask2 on the Actor passed in RDX. Limitations: Only descriptor/data references were found; do not infer a publicly callable generic toggle contract.
Sets Actor+288 mask2 but also clears movement vectors and requests native motion/action0xA1. Limitations: Not called as a trainer separation setter because its other side effects are substantial.

Frees the dynamic-node pool and nulls its pool pointer while leaving dynamic list head/tail uncleared in this body. Limitations: Nonnull list roots can be stale after teardown; never dereference a cached dynamic contact from readability alone.

Performs map/scene subsystem teardown, including dynamic-pool release before later asset unloads. Limitations: Confirms transition-time lifetime loss; a scene-ready/heap/scheduler lease must be revalidated.

Skips normal collision/update work for native stopped/frozen or special action paths while other maintenance can continue. Limitations: Cached contact data has no proven per-frame freshness token; diagnostics are explicitly last-evaluated results.

Resolves collision-group enable/disable through Actor action/group bitsets then collision-resource defaults. Limitations: Do not assign friendly names to undocumented group indices or indiscriminately enable all shapes.
Iterates20-byte source entries by exact type, with22 as a wildcard selector. Limitations: The separate3C9BC0 iterator uses type masks and must not be conflated with this API.

Prize processing uses the same3BA970 body gate on prize actors in its attraction/pickup path. Limitations: Global application of the separation bit could affect prizes; the new feature changes only the validated current Sora.
Another prize update path checks the native body-separation gate before attraction/pickup processing. Limitations: No universal 'noclip all actors' control is proposed.

Uses transformed model bounds normally; the40AC20 multi-shape bounds fallback is used when model+2696 is absent and a body buffer exists. Limitations: The MINSS anomaly is limited to this fallback, not asserted for all rendered actors.
A separate movement/separation pass iterates other actors and honors3BA970 on the relevant body buffers. Limitations: The mask2 control affects these verified separation consumers, not hit detection.

Motion worker removes queued callback/context/index triples under its mutex, invokes each callback, then signals its completion semaphore only after the queue is empty. Limitations: A static ordering guarantee for this native worker loop; arbitrary mods can change scheduling.
Waits on and releases all six worker completion semaphores at112-byte stride before returning. Limitations: Together with130030 this establishes the normal post-motion completion barrier.

Acquires all worker completion semaphores, distributes24-byte job triples across six workers under queue mutexes, then wakes every worker. Limitations: The input callback ABI is contextRCX/indexEDX, confirmed by the worker callsite.

Increments waiter count, calls WaitForSingleObject(handle+8,INFINITE), then decrements waiter count. Limitations: Used as the completion wait primitive; no timeout/error recovery beyond native behavior is inferred.
Tailcalls ReleaseSemaphore(handle+8,1,null). Limitations: A synchronization primitive, not a lifetime allocator.
Reads Actor pointer from context array at indexEDX and tailcalls3BFAB0 with Actor in RCX. Limitations: Confirms the motion-worker callback ABI and Actor argument ownership.

Native stop predicate checks timed stop+1612, category-dependent stop, Actor+288 mask0x400 and global stop context38EE40. Limitations: The implemented cache filter excludes these known stop branches conservatively; no complete frame-freshness claim.
Returns numeric flag1 from the timed-state byte pointed to by RCX. Limitations: Used at Actor+1612 by the stop predicate.

Returns true if global stop contextBF2AC8 has any nonzero QWORD among four lanes at+80..104. Limitations: The readout checks these lanes without calling the native routine; unknown/unreadable context suppresses contact interpretation.

Initializes the movement block pointed to by RCX: relative+0 walk2, +4 run8, +8 fallback jump160, +12 angular value, +16 fall cap loaded from parameter table+20, +20 zero. The fall cap is data-driven. Limitations: The parameter initializer is not a safe general reset: it also resets unrelated movement fields.

Actor construction calls40A440 at Actor+296 while resetting movement, physics, script and stop-control state. Limitations: Large constructor has many resource requirements; the trainer only edits four proven fields on an existing actor.

Normal input chooses Actor+296 below analog magnitude0.8 and Actor+300 at/above0.8, storing the selected speed in Actor+28. Special Action IDs2/24/53 and Action flag8 use other paths; flag8 uses Actor+316. Limitations: These are normal movement parameters, not universal speed multipliers for every Action.
Two-instruction base-player input wrapper moves actor RDX to RCX and tail-jumps3A8FA0. Limitations: Current Sora uses its own equivalent wrapper404FB0.

Sora input wrapper moves RDX to RCX and tail-jumps the shared3A8FA0 movement-input consumer. Limitations: Static descriptor750300/vtable5CBA28 slot296 identity is pinned by the trainer; no callback is patched.

An alternate input helper reads the same walk/run fields and threshold0.8 before updating Actor+28. Limitations: Its complete call-site reachability was not established; primary Sora proof uses404FB0.

Movement helper uses selected input magnitude Actor+28 and input vector+16, blends against existing velocity+32, and returns the movement vector. Limitations: Native float argument registers and scaling make the historical decompiler prototype unreliable; the trainer does not call this function.

Sora constructor calls base-player initialization with the requested form argument and then installs the same descriptor750300 independently of form. Limitations: Resource-specific Actions may still override movement. Support is restricted to established Sora forms0..6, not special characters/forms.

VM adapter decodes an object handle then its actor, returns an encoded pointer to Actor+296, exposing the movement parameter block to scripts. Limitations: This proves script access can overwrite one-time values; no claim that static direct-writer enumeration covers all generic VM memory stores.

Reads Actor+304 as fallback jump height and defaults output motionID3. When eligible and positive High Jump level exists, it uses the growth-table height and motion201. Limitations: Changing base height does not override an enabled High Jump growth level.
Returns the same fallback or growth-table jump height without the output motion ID. Limitations: This is a selector, not a writable single resolved-height field.

Copies movement input to a vector and fills its vertical component from3B59B0; optional flag sets Actor flags288 bit0x10000. Limitations: This is one jump preparation path and does not prove every jump Action consumes the base parameter.

Prepares a normal jump using resolved height/motion, calls the native vector jump initializer and selects motion, then sets Actor state fields280/284. Limitations: Trainer changes the parameter for subsequent consumers; it does not force this Action or restart a jump.

ABI RCX=Actor and XMM1=height. Configures jump elapsed/peak/base/delta fields240..252; positive height becomes negative vertical delta and duration derives from sqrt(2*height/g). Limitations: Calling this alone would bypass Action transitions. No engine call is exposed.

Jump motion computes eased ascent or quadratic descent with constant0.40816328, then caps vertical displacement with timeStep*Actor+312. Limitations: The cap is not a gravity multiplier. Historical prototype does not represent float register ABI accurately.

Full ASM establishes output in RDX, Actor in R8 and timestep XMM3; elapsed time advances, vertical result is min(targetY-currentY, timestep*Actor+312), and downward-state flag is updated. Limitations: Positive downward speed is native coordinate behavior. Special motion flags bypass vertical movement.
Computes the corresponding vertical displacement from existing elapsed/peak values and caps it with timestep*Actor+312. Limitations: Does not itself advance elapsed time; trainer does not call it.

Air-action update applies per-frame0.40816328 acceleration, caps vertical velocity by Actor+312, then scales output displacement by timestep. Limitations: Additional action parameters affect horizontal/upward behavior. No universal adjustable gravity global is demonstrated.

ABI RCX=Actor, EDX=stopID, XMM2=duration; if Actor+2488 bit4 is clear, forwards to stop-control block Actor+1612. Limitations: Not implemented: table and four-slot capacity validation are necessary before a native call.

VM bank6/index6 adapter decodes actor and forwards integer stop ID plus float duration to3B6730 in the actual native registers. Limitations: VM metadata arg_count3 and ASM distinguish the float third argument omitted in older pseudocode.

Searches four stop slots for a matching ID or empty slot, writes ID/duration, then ORs flags from3EED10 for every active slot. Limitations: With four different occupied IDs the selected slot pointer can remain null. Missing table rows are also dereferenced; unchecked use is unsafe.

Ticks positive stop timers using global tick factor717480, clears expired IDs and recomputes the aggregate stop mask. Limitations: Nonpositive timers are not automatically expired; a persistent actor-freeze feature would require ownership and removal policy.

Clears matching stop IDs among four slots and recomputes aggregate flags for remaining IDs. Limitations: Removing an ID also owned by a game script would affect its stop; no override API is currently exposed.
Looks up stop metadata in a loaded sorted four-byte row table at2AE59D8, with row count from header+4. Limitations: The concrete stop-ID-to-mask contents were not loaded or proven in this round.

Actor stop predicate combines stop-control maskbit1, category/global conditions, Actor flags288 bit0x400 and another global state. Limitations: Actor flags288 bit0x400 is also used by visibility paths; it is not a clean AI-only pause bit.

Main Actor update calls descriptor pre-update+8 before stop-timer/predicate checks. A stopped actor skips central motion/controller/physics updates but retains maintenance and render-list handling. Limitations: Because pre-update still runs, the mechanism is not established as complete AI/BDX suspension.

Traverses live actors and applies a supplied stop ID with duration0 only to actor categorybit0x10. Limitations: This is a native enemy-category stop path; record table contents and ownership are still needed for a trainer feature.
Traverses actors and removes a supplied stop ID from each actor's stop-control block. Limitations: Global removal could undo script-owned state; it is documented rather than exposed.

Script-context gate checks its+300 bit1 and current motion/reaction predicates on the decoded actor. Limitations: Not identified as an independent AI pause setter; changing it would need additional state-machine proof.

Accepts menu level1..10, constructs bus controller1, applies the indexed float from RVA5AB960 with duration0, then destroys the temporary wrapper. Limitations: No level0 call is applied here. The numeric bus identity is established; its audible content still depends on routing.

Accepts level1..10 and applies the same table gain to bus3 when8BBD14 is nonzero, otherwise bus2, and then buses4,5,6,7,8. Limitations: This changes several bus gains; it is not a per-voice fade and should not be treated as an atomic multi-bus transaction.

Accepts level1..10; with8BBD14 nonzero it sets bus2. Otherwise it sets bus3 and additionally multiplies the table gain by the float at5AAA40 when8BBD18 is nonzero. Limitations: The extra flag-dependent branch is present in full ASM but omitted from the older cached pseudocode.

ABI is bus-ID-pointer inRCX, gainfloat inXMM1, durationnumerator inR8D and denominator inR9D. It computes300000*numerator/denominator using signed integer arithmetic, constructs a bus controller and calls07FA10 with a pointer to the converted duration. Limitations: Zero denominator and signed overflow are not guarded; this wrapper is not suitable for arbitrary frontend arguments.

ABI is unsigned busID inECX and floatgain inXMM1. It constructs079C90's temporary controller, calls07FAD0(controller,gain,0), then07F7E0. There is no branch that stops playback when gain is zero. Limitations: Immediate zero-duration setters can call backend/voice iteration; lifetime, routing and restore policy must be established before a trainer call.

Under the global sound critical section, controllerID0 selects master2B811D0; a positive bounded ID selects table2B811C8[id-1]. The chosen object's virtual slot24 receives gainXMM1 and durationR8D. Limitations: Caller must validate finite gain and a supported live backend; the critical section does not independently prove driver lifetime.

Converts the signed duration pointed to byR8 from300000ticks per second into integer milliseconds, then resolves controllerID to master/child bus under the sound critical section and calls virtual slot24 with gain and duration. Limitations: Integer conversion/truncation changes short durations. No high-level channel identity is implied by a controllerID.

Temporary BusController destructor only resets the wrapper's vtable to61ACD0 and returns. Limitations: This body does not own or release the bus object and does not prove a persistent wrapper can survive backend teardown.

Constructs a controller under the sound critical section via SoundDriver vtable+152. If the driver is absent, it writes the BusController vtable, ID-1 and null backend. Limitations: The caller's wrapper storage must cover all fields written. A successfully constructed wrapper is not a bus-lifetime lease.

The base SoundDriver bus-controller constructor stores requestedID atout+8, BusController vtable atout+0 and current2B81DE8 backend atout+16. Limitations: This body performs no range or bus-existence check.

Bus gain setter writes target+36. With nonzero duration it updates interpolation fields+40,+44,+48,+52,+61 only. With zero duration it writes current+32 and walks the bus or referenced bus's voice list under its own critical section to propagate combined gain. Limitations: The nonzero duration lower28bits must be positive; flag bits alone cause division by zero. Deferred updates still depend on native bus/voice lifetime.

XA2 master gain setter takes THIS inRCX, floatgainXMM1 and durationR8D. Nonzero duration updates interpolation fields; zero duration calls mastering voice virtual+96 when present and stores current/target gain, clearing remaining duration. Limitations: Zero gain is a volume value here, not a playback-stop branch. Backend voice lifetime and native return status need runtime validation.

Generic master gain setter uses the same interpolation layout. Its immediate branch updates current gain and writes inherited gain+56 and dirty+60 for each child bus counted bymaster+344. Limitations: The immediate branch assumes the child pointer array and its count are coherent.
Reads the native settings block via14CDE0 and applies unsigned16-bit field+22 through137D50. Limitations: This wrapper applies current settings; it does not itself write or persist a new setting.
Reads settings field+24 and applies it through138290, the multi-bus gain routine. Limitations: Not a standalone save or configuration-file writer.
Reads settings field+26 and applies it through138440, including its routing/attenuation flags. Limitations: Not a standalone save or configuration-file writer.

Implements audio pause/duck/restore over music entries plus buses2,3,5,6,7,8. Mode1 records ownership atmusicEntry+60 and pauses; mode2 halves remembered gain when not paused; mode0 resumes only owned paused entries or restores remembered gain. Limitations: Calling this directly would overlap the game's existing pause stack. It does not provide an independent trainer-owned pause layer.

Pushes the requested sound-pause mode onto the DWORD stack atAD8030 using countAD803C, applies1DF710(mode), then increments count. Limitations: This body does not check stack capacity and should not be used as a repeatedly refreshed toggle.
Pops one entry from the sound-pause mode stack when nonempty, then applies the new top mode orzero via1DF710. Limitations: A trainer must not pop a pause pushed by gameplay or another component.

Effective bus gain is the product of three DynamicValue stages atobject+24,+64,+104, with each getter potentially applying its own inherited multiplier. Limitations: Reading only current+32 reports one gain stage, not final audible volume or perceived loudness.

The music-path resolver remaps tracks 117→517 and 121→521 in world 13. It adds 400 to tracks 106–109 and 113 when module mode is neither 0 nor 7, or the guarded option bit returned by 2E5410 is set; formats into one shared buffer at AD93E0. Limitations: The shared buffer is overwritten by the next call. These are conditional asset IDs, not a complete music catalogue.
Returns the current module-mode DWORD at RVA 716750. Limitations: Names of every mode are not established by this getter.
Returns bit 0 of BEDF10 only while module mode is 0 or 7, otherwise returns false. Limitations: The user-facing option name is not established here.
Forwards channel and gain to 1DF310 after multiplying the supplied duration by eight. Limitations: Gain units and time conversion come from the callee, not from the wrapper alone.
Forwards a selected channel, zero gain and the supplied duration to 1DF310. Limitations: Zero gain follows a stop/fade-out path; this is not reversible muting.

Converts an integer gain to float gain/16383 and duration from 240 units/second to integer milliseconds, then calls 1388F0. Limitations: The wrapper does not range-check channel, negative gain or duration.

Normalizes both EDX and R8D integer gains by 16383, puts them in XMM1/XMM2 and converts R9D duration to milliseconds before tail-calling 138AB0. Limitations: Hex-Rays omits the XMM1 float in its current inferred prototype. Calling it with that inferred integer ABI is incorrect.

Looks for a channel-tagged active entry (ID+48/type+62). It resumes an existing paused handle or keeps an already active one; otherwise creates a 72-byte entry from a matching loaded bank and links it into the active list. ABI: channel ECX, initial gain XMM1, target gain XMM2, milliseconds R9D; target gain is retained at entry+64. Limitations: It requires an already loaded bank. There is no arbitrary-track asset load here; native list/heap ownership must be respected.

Returns activity of the first matching channel/type-1 entry by querying its sound handle through 081EB0; returns false when driver or entry is absent. Limitations: This is a boolean activity test, not playback position or completion progress.

Finds the first matching channel/type-1 active entry. Positive gain calls handle volume interpolation 082140; nonpositive gain calls stop/fade-out 0818B0. Limitations: Using gain zero for a trainer mute would stop playback and could not be undone by merely restoring volume.

Stops the matching music handle, removes its entry from the singly linked active list, updates tail/count, clears its next pointer, and invokes its deleting destructor. Limitations: The operation destroys an owned entry; retaining it across a stop/track change is unsafe.
Tail wrapper for the channel stop/remove routine 138D20. Limitations: No independent ownership or null-safety beyond the callee.

Converts duration from 240 units/second to milliseconds and reaches the channel pause dispatch at 1389C0, which matches ID/type and calls 081B70. Limitations: The reported function disassembly contains only the entry wrapper; the tail body is separately addressed. This is not complete low-level audio pause semantics.
Returns the low-byte result of sound-load-queue activity helper 1E0130. Limitations: Only the pending-load query is established; it does not identify a playable sound.

Dequeues a free 48-byte load-request record from the pool indexed by 728E40, stores callback/context/channel/type/data/size and appends it with packed next pointers. Limitations: The allocator decrements the free count without an entry guard in this body. A trainer must not blindly enqueue through it.

Stops the target channel, allocates an aligned buffer for a named asset, starts loading, yields its task while loading is active, submits the sound-data request, yields again until the queue completes, then frees the buffer. Limitations: It requires a valid yielding task context. Calling it directly from the trainer's outer update callback would not establish that requirement.

Processes pending per-channel flags to load channel 0/1 music through a task context and selects fade/start behavior based on current activity and event state. Limitations: This claim covers dispatch and ownership only; every event/crossfade condition is not yet mapped to a user-facing meaning.
Writes the requested track ID into ABAD44 + channel*16. Limitations: No channel bound check exists in this setter.
Writes the current-track bookkeeping field into ABAD40 + channel*16. Limitations: Changing this field alone does not load or start music.
Writes the channel scalar/bookkeeping field at ABAD48 + channel*16. Limitations: A direct field edit does not establish audio gain application.

Builds a channel-0 load request for music ID 142 in the supplied task context and calls the yielding loader 1DF1D0. Limitations: The specific scene purpose of this hard-coded music choice is not established.

Builds a type-6 event resource load using a signed track ID from the command; special mode 0x400000 uses an aligned staging allocation and asynchronous completion callback. Limitations: Event resource ownership and task-yielding requirements preclude direct use as a simple trainer button.

Resolves a type-6 loaded event resource, changes channel track bookkeeping, and queues its memory through 1E03E0. A command channel value of 2 updates both channel bookkeeping records. Limitations: Native event object structure and lifecycle are required; not a safe arbitrary-channel UI API.

Initializes global Sound critical section at RVA 2B81278 and registers 571EB0 as an exit callback. Limitations: Process initialization, not a scene-ready flag.
Deletes global Sound critical section at process exit. Limitations: Must not invoke Sound APIs from DLL detach or after CRT teardown.

Finds the first type-1 entry with matching channel in list RVA 713470 and queries its SoundController at entry+16 through 081EB0. Limitations: Only establishes current activity; no ownership, no bank loading, no list lock in this wrapper.

Converts the original duration/channel arguments and jumps into shared tail RVA 1389C0; that tail searches the music list and calls 081B70 with the duration from R8D. Limitations: 1389C0 is a shared function chunk, not an independent conventional two-argument API. Its live decompile is attributed to canonical function 1DC390.

For matching music entry, gain<=0 calls native stop 0818B0; positive gain calls 082140. This wrapper cannot implement a mute that preserves playback. Limitations: Does not change the entry+64 stored baseline gain used by global pause/duck.

Pauses a resolved SoundController: RCX=controller, EDX=unsigned milliseconds. Enters global CS then backend/layout lock; positive handle calls voice vtable+48, negative handle calls 0384E0. Limitations: EDX is a duration, not a bool. No validity return or controller lifetime ownership is provided.

Sets gain on an existing SoundController with RCX=controller, XMM1=float gain, R8D=milliseconds. Rejects non-finite input and resolves the backend under global and backend locks. Limitations: Decompiler loses float register forwarding at the virtual call; dedicated ASM verifies it. This API alone is not a persistent bus setting.

Queries current SoundController activity under global and backend/layout locking after handle resolution. Limitations: Activity is distinct from the paused query 081FF0; do not use this result as pause ownership.

Native bus-gain wrapper constructs a BusController from *RCX, takes float in XMM1 and duration/rate in R8D/R9D, converts duration then calls 07FA10. Limitations: Only metadata xref was found. Caller-controlled rate0 and integer arithmetic make this a worse trainer entry point than 07FAD0.

Resolves BusController ID0 to the master and IDs1..count to list[id-1], then sets bus gain through vtable+24 under the global Sound CS. Duration is read from an integer pointer and converted from 300000 units/second to milliseconds. Limitations: Does not itself validate float finiteness or guarantee that bus globals are outside teardown.

MasterBusXA2 gain setter has RCX=master, XMM1=float gain, R8D=encoded milliseconds. Nonzero duration updates DynamicValue fields only; zero updates the XA2 voice volume directly and current/target fields. Limitations: Gain zero follows SetVolume/envelope logic, not native SoundController Stop. Actual audio output depends on subsequent backend updates.

Constructs a 24-byte stack BusController by driver virtual+152 under the global CS; absent driver gives ID=-1 and null layout. Limitations: Controller is a non-owning selector; it does not extend driver, bus, or layout lifetime.

Native bus gain setter: RCX=BusController*, XMM1=float gain, R8D=milliseconds. It resolves current global bus/master and dispatches vtable+24 under global CS. Limitations: Use finite 0..1 and duration1 for a candidate trainer operation. Locks do not protect the separately serialized teardown by themselves.
BusController destructor only writes its class vtable. Limitations: No backend refcount or lifetime pin is acquired/released by this stack wrapper.

Ordinary Bus gain setter uses target+36,current+32,step+40,remaining+44,total+48,start+52,curve+61. Nonzero duration writes envelope fields; zero immediately traverses voices under bus+280 lock and applies their composite gain. Limitations: A 1 ms request avoids an immediate voice-list walk but still needs current driver/bus lifetime.

Generic MasterBus gain setter interpolates when duration is nonzero; immediate mode writes current gain and each child bus's parent multiplier/dirty state. Limitations: This is a gain stage, not a transport stop/pause. Generic and XA2 master implementations have different immediate propagation paths.

Resolves a controller ID; positive IDs query the current backend voice under the pool lock and may map through virtual+560, while unresolved IDs fall back to the stored signed ID. Limitations: A controller includes a layout pointer for negative IDs; copying the struct is not a lifetime guarantee.

Validates positive voice IDs against their active-list membership and virtual+648 full-ID check after deriving a pool slot from ID&0x1ff. Limitations: Index alone is insufficient; the full generation-bearing ID and native resolver must be retained.

Resumes a SoundController with RCX=controller and EDX=milliseconds, using matching global/backend or layout locks; positive voice virtual+64, negative 0385A0. Limitations: Resume should not be issued to undo an unrelated menu/global pause.

Queries whether the resolved SoundController is paused, under global and backend/layout locks; positive virtual+640, negative layout voice state bit2. Limitations: Reports state, not which caller owns the pause.

Checks whether a SoundController resolves to a currently valid positive pool voice or negative layout voice under global CS. Limitations: Validation is a momentary query; re-resolve immediately for an operation and do not retain raw backend pointers.

Destroys a music/SFX entry by destructing its embedded SoundController, replacing its joint vtable, and freeing on the deleting flag. Limitations: Cached raw active-entry pointers can become invalid during regular cleanup, even without scene or driver teardown.

Creates/publishes the 72-byte AxaSoundManager singleton at RVA 8BBD08, initializing inherited thread handles to zero and manager state. Limitations: CThread inheritance alone is not evidence that this manager list is always processed on a separate thread.

Destroys and clears AxaSoundManager, removes loaded banks, resets bank-list globals, and frees auxiliary storage. Limitations: This function does not by itself establish that every active-entry global was nulled before destruction.

Walks active entries, removes and destroys those that are invalid or inactive, then cleans bank/stream state. Limitations: Only walk this high-level list in a proven serialized engine lifecycle point; low-level sound CS does not automatically cover the list.

Registers the Sound update callback 1DC370 on outer scheduler RVA 9BA888 with priority500010 during sound setup. Limitations: This proves an engine-scheduler cleanup path; it does not prove the absence of other callers or backend worker threads.

Scheduled Sound callback calls 1DD8D0,1DF440,13C470 in order. Limitations: Callback registration and code together identify a regular cleanup boundary, not a license to call yielding resource loaders.

Native global audio pause/duck/resume coordinates music entry+60 flags, stored gain+64 and manager+68, and bus pause/resume calls. Limitations: A trainer must respect the existing global pause owner. Blind resume can defeat a game/menu pause; gain restoration can overwrite native ducking if the wrong stage is used.

Stops active audio and joins backend workers before destroying helper objects and the SoundDriver; driver global is nulled only after its deleting destructor returns. Limitations: Final driver/bus destruction is not enclosed in the global Sound CS. Runtime pointer checks alone leave a teardown race for arbitrary worker callers.

Cleanup variant joins audio worker threads, then destroys/nuls helpers and driver and clears XA2 initialization state. Limitations: Same lifetime boundary as normal teardown; do not use the CS as a universal ownership lock.

Resets the global bus/master state, creates a 424-byte MasterBusXA2, creates ordinary buses, then binds master's child-list pointer+336 and count+344. Limitations: Driver/master/list identity can change across initialization; no old bus pointer may be carried across it.

Builds ordinary buses using configured count, allocates the pointer array and 336-byte bus objects, assigns each ID=index+1. Limitations: Trainer must bound IDs by actual count and validate every selected object; an arbitrary number is not a valid bus.

Creates a MasterBusXA2 from the current audio configuration and publishes it to global RVA 2B811D0. Limitations: Master identity can change independently of a stored controller ID. Bind and recheck the master pointer itself.

SoundDriver deleting destructor drains/releases backend resources, calls 08FA20 for buses and deletes its instance critical section before freeing itself. Limitations: Global driver pointer is still nonzero while its destructor runs; it cannot alone prove a stable object.

Computes a composite bus multiplier from three DynamicValues, including the first stage's parent multiplier at+56. Limitations: Do not use this composite getter as the original value for restoring only the first gain stage; save stage target/current fields instead.

MasterBusXA2 regular update advances the gain DynamicValue and sends its evaluated gain to the XA2 voice SetVolume slot. Limitations: Confirms a nonzero-duration setter is applied by the regular update path. No live audibility test was performed.

Bus regular update validates/removes dead controllers, advances gain envelopes, computes composite gain and applies it to voices under the bus list lock. Limitations: The update can enter global Sound CS while holding the bus lock. Preserve native scheduling/locking order; do not introduce a worker that holds global CS across arbitrary bus/list work.

Destroys normal buses, frees global bus-list storage and destroys the master; it does not clear global bus-list pointer, count or master pointer. Limitations: This is concrete evidence of temporarily dangling global bus pointers during destruction. Memory readability and expected vtable are insufficient lifecycle proofs.

Stops one audio worker by setting its exit byte, waiting indefinitely on its thread handle, closing it, then destroying and nulling worker state. Limitations: Teardown synchronization is join-based; no trainer call should be made from an audio shutdown callback.

Stops the second audio worker using exit byte, thread join, handle close and object destruction. Limitations: Backend activity is multi-threaded even though high-level cleanup has an engine scheduler callback.
SoundController destructor only restores the SoundController vtable. Limitations: A copied controller struct does not own the voice or the negative-ID layout.

Evaluates a DynamicValue using current/target/start/remaining/total fields and curve kind; curve0 returns current directly. Limitations: For a linear 1 ms override, save the original stable target, not a transient composite or nonlinear evaluated value.

Driver constructs BusController by writing ID at+8, vtable at+0 and auxiliary layout pointer at+16. Limitations: The result contains selectors only; it has no bus pointer, generation token or refcount.

Orders application Init virtual+8, repeated Update virtual+32, and Shutdown virtual+40 on the same call stack. Update must finish before shutdown is invoked. Limitations: Covers the observed native application loop; does not authorize calls from arbitrary trainer workers or DLL detach.

Application initialization calls13C910 when required, then builds the engine task manager; audio initialization precedes ordinary update frames. Limitations: The caller must retain the verified application identity.

Runs the outer task manager and returns0 for continued frames or2 to leave the loop. Existing trainer post-update can reject nonzero returns. Limitations: The audio contract requires the continued-frame branch and known engine thread.
Application shutdown reaches13C7C0 and returns1, preventing another ordinary frame in this native shutdown sequence. Limitations: No trainer operation is valid during this callback.
Creates the sound manager only when global8BBD08 is null, first calling1437B0 to construct the sound backend. Limitations: A singleton nonnull test alone is not a lifetime proof.

Destroys/nulls sound manager8BBD08, clears game sound-bank lists/configuration, and calls143770 for backend shutdown. Limitations: Some destruction occurs outside global Sound CS; the application-loop ordering is essential.

Conditionally enters077BE0 from normal manager teardown and frees initialization storage. Limitations: Alternate initialization mode8BBDA0 changes this branch.
Runs audio configuration/backend initialization and reaches076F20; failure paths set silent/failure flags. Limitations: Graph validation remains necessary even after application initialization.
Allocates SoundDriver only when2B81DE0 is null and publishes auxiliary backend objects. Limitations: No observed ordinary frame caller replaces a live driver through this function.

Clears audio roots, constructs MasterXA2 and normal buses, and binds master+336 to bus-list2B811C8 and master+344 DWORD to count2B811A4. Limitations: Initialization code; do not call to implement a mixer reset.
Settings/menu initialization can call13C910, whose singleton guard preserves an already initialized backend. Limitations: This does not demonstrate a hot audio device reset.

Alternative initialization configuration calls076E50 and sets8BBDA0. Limitations: Only unwind metadata references were found; no runtime entry through normal callers, PE pointers, CLR methods or exports was established.

Wrapper reaches076F20 to construct absent backend objects. Limitations: Its only normal caller is077500; no live runtime entry to that wrapper was identified.

Allocates a new MasterXA2 and replaces master-root2B811D0. Its sole RVA data occurrence is the .pdata RUNTIME_FUNCTION08DB30..08DC78 with unwind6975B0. Timer callback calls077FC0 with elapsed-time sentinel-1. Limitations: No trainer call should be injected into the timer callback.

Sets the per-process failure-stage message and progress1, creates the managed process exit table, executes __xc_mp_a..__xc_mp_z via _initterm_m, then sets progress2 and DefaultDomain.InitializedPerProcess. Sets the per-AppDomain failure-stage message and progress1, calls _initatexit_app_domain, executes __xc_ma_a..__xc_ma_z and records progress2. The exit-table initialization return is discarded; this binary's seven nonzero table entries clear the seven CurrentDomain fields individually.

Sets the uninitializer failure-stage message, creates an EventHandler for LanguageSupport.DomainUnload and registers it with ModuleUninitializer. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. Registration is part of the final initialization stage; this body does not unload anything immediately.

Records whether the current AppDomain is default and sets the process Entered flag. It acquires the native startup lock with the current fiber ID, tolerates recursive acquisition by the same ID and retries others after Sleep(1000). Under that lock it initializes vtables and default-domain native/per-process state; another domain can request default-domain initialization after releasing the lock. It then initializes per-domain state, marks the domain initialized and registers its uninitializer. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. Lock release is protected by finally and occurs only for the outer owner. This orchestrates runtime/module startup, not a callable feature toggle; calling it again manually would violate the compiler-owned lifecycle.

Delegates per-AppDomain teardown to _app_exit_callback. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. It does not independently guarantee once-only execution; DomainUnload supplies that guard.

Runs the process exit callback and clears InitializedPerProcess. If native initialization was performed by the module cctor, calls _cexit, clears native startup state and the ownership flag. Finally clears InitializedNative and returns zero. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. The ownership flag prevents this path from treating all native startup as cctor-owned. Callback exceptions can interrupt later cleanup steps.

If the default domain was entered, uninitializes directly when already in that domain; otherwise invokes the native default-domain teardown thunk with a null cookie through DoCallBackInDefaultDomain. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. The thunk field stores native VA0x140579E90. No action occurs when the Entered flag is false.

Skips uninitialized domains and uses Interlocked.Exchange(Uninitialized,1) as an exactly-once gate. The first entrant decrements the shared domain count, tears down the current domain and, when the count becomes zero, uninitializes default-domain/process state. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. If teardown throws, the once flag and decremented count are not rolled back. The guard belongs to this handler, not to ModuleUninitializer's stack enumerator.

Failure cleanup decrements the shared domain count, runs per-domain teardown and tears down process/default-domain state when last. Cleanup exceptions are wrapped together with the original initialization exception; the non-Exception catch supplies a null secondary exception. Limitations: Synthetic CIL address, not a native RVA or process-call address. This is the failed-initialization path; callers must only use it after the successful domain-count increment. RCX is Mission*, EDX unsigned mission ID, R8 filename token. Constructor builds msn/<language>/<token>.bar; initializes one timer+296, three counters+352 with stride80, three gauges+592 with stride72, watch+808, combo counter+880, score+1088, phase+1072=0 and Drive factor+1704=1. The decompiler's apparent two-argument prototype omits R8. Limitations: The resource token and ID list are external mission data. Constructor flags1 alone do not establish widget configuration.

Reconstructs the mission in static storage RVA2A0F8B0 and publishes the returned pointer in RVA2A0FF68. The incoming filename in RDX becomes constructor R8. Limitations: Pointer equality alone is not a lifetime/generation token; identical missions can reuse storage.

Attaches loaded BAR at Mission+96, obtains BAR type2 descriptor into Mission+8 and mirror RVA2A0FF70, and translates descriptor flags1/20/40/80/100 into native control state. Limitations: Missing BAR entries can be dereferenced in native code; not an arbitrary trainer loader API.

Parses descriptor commands beginning at+28, loads optional BAR type3 script/type18 effects, starts presentation and registers3A35C0 as group1 priority14000 task. Limitations: This owns resources and task allocation; not reused by timer actions.

Descriptor opcode4 configures timer;5 counter;6 gauge;7 combo;8 score;9 watch. Opcode11 stores mission Drivefactor+1704;12 adjusts current Drive through native status helper. Limitations: Record IDs and lengths are not bounds-checked by these dispatch arms; loaded resources are an engine trust assumption.

Initializes the specified widget through vtable+8, configures start/max/threshold through+48, optionally attaches BAR HUD resources, appends widget to Mission+976 registry and increments count+1048. Limitations: Registry capacity is nine pointers before count1048. Trainer independently rejects out-of-bounds, duplicate or foreign entries.
Counter descriptor index at record+19 selects Mission+352+80*index. Limitations: Trainer accepts only the three statically constructed counters.

Gauge descriptor index selects Mission+592+72*index, configures it and calls3FA310 with float-converted initial value. Limitations: Initialization itself can follow setter threshold behavior. Trainer does not call it.
Timer descriptor index selects Mission+296+56*index. Limitations: Only one timer is constructed; trainer requires index0, exact timer vtable and registry membership.

Default base widget reset sets flags1, ID fromEDX, max0, sound0 and UI resource null. Limitations: Unused inline widgets therefore still have bit1; publishing their old +56 fields without registry/ID checks would be wrong.
Activates each registered widget via vtable+16 except objects with flag0x10, then sets Mission flags bit1. Limitations: Mission active flag is separate from per-widget active flag4.
Stops all registered widgets via vtable+24 and clears Mission flags bit1. Limitations: Do not restart timers when the mission's native UI/control set is intentionally stopped.
Calls widget stop when active and sets flag0x10 to suppress subsequent automatic activation. Limitations: Timer action rejects this state instead of overriding hidden/disabled native ownership.

Mission phase0 starts widgets when its presentation permits; phase1 is the ordinary active state. Phase2 advances to3; phase3 sets up terminal presentation and advances4; phase4 eventually dispatches saved event+1076 and argument+1080, then ends its task. Limitations: Exact names of events7/16 are not inferred from the integers alone.

Member-style lifecycle updater mirrors3A35C0 and passes both saved event and argument to3A3540; returns false after terminal dispatch. Limitations: Only scheduler-registered3A35C0 is relied on for the current native path.

Returns true when current mission exists and Mission flags bit4 is clear. Limitations: This native gate alone is weaker than trainer guards: it does not prove phase1, initialized timer, pause state or scene safety.
Tests only whether global current mission pointer is nonnull. Limitations: Presence is not resource/configuration readiness.
Returns current Mission pointer without validation. Limitations: Module uses direct checked reads; it does not expose this pointer to users.
Loader cleanup clears current mission pointer and descriptor mirror. Limitations: Mission destructor does not alone clear every resource field in static storage.

Teardown stops clock, applies mission-specific cleanup, destroys script/effect resource handles, releases BAR and nulls current mission. Certain mission IDs also check counters for a Steam achievement before cleanup. Limitations: Counter edits can influence achievements; mission data is not merely a display.
Returns Mission+1704 float if a mission exists, otherwise1. Limitations: Corrects earlier shorthand: RVA2A0FF68 is Mission, not a generic area structure. No new Drive control is implemented here.
Tests descriptor flag0x1000 from Mission+8,+4. Limitations: Root separately studies how this gates retry checkpoint creation; this module does not change it.
Reports whether Mission flags0x10 is clear, or true if no mission exists. Limitations: This is a control/finish gate, not an independent lifecycle generation.
ORs supplied mask into Mission+1696 when mission exists. Limitations: Potential future standard-gauge-update hold; no persistent mask override implemented.
Clears only supplied mask from Mission+1696. Limitations: A future lease must preserve other owners and account for mission reconstruction, direct setter bypasses and third-party writers.

Activates counter flag4 and creates optional HUD bound to live value+56 and maximum+36. Existing completed flag8 selects completed presentation. Limitations: Readouts never dereference the HUD pointer.

Constructor receives controller in RCX and Actor in RDX, sets owner+16 and speed+336 tofloat1. Actor embeds the controller at+344, so speed is Actor+680. Logical/resolved IDs initialize to-1. Motion/resource replacement resets duration/frame/blend/trigger state but does not reset speed+336. Therefore speed ownership is Actor-wide, and a per-motion lease that simply expires would leak the override. Limitations: Unknown modded writers can change this behavior. Normal motion/resource identity changes are allowed only with a valid fresh supported View and unchanged Actor/model identities.

Original performs no validation; wrapper always forwards its behavior exactly once.

Limitations: Model/resource/header guards establish a plausible current engine object, not validation of every recursively referenced bone/IK asset buffer.

Reads loaded color-vision type at Settings+16 and severity+18. Disabled becomes(0,0), enabled severity clamps1..10; type remains unchecked. Limitations: Explicit restore should snapshot/validate all three display settings and then call the preview APIs with that immutable snapshot.

Fullscreen enqueue captures target/program/source and renderer into a native closure and passes it to119BA0. Limitations: Borrowed render resources and replay closures prevent safely substituting arbitrary targets from the host.

Limitations: Synchronization is supplied by its outer callers, not by this function itself. Xrefs are finite static evidence, not a proof against external code.

Normal presentation path acquires the in-situ MSVCP mutex at GX+30848 before rendering/replay/frame completion, and unlocks it on the normal return path. Limitations: Use the same runtime import and native lifecycle. Do not reinterpret the opaque mutex as a Windows CRITICAL_SECTION.

Timing thread takes the same GX+30848 mutex around its intermediate-frame replay/completion. It can run while the application update thread is active. Limitations: Scalar atomicity alone is insufficient for coupled preview fields. Worker lifetime and renderer teardown still need gating.

Replay temporarily sets GX+22944, interpolates camera data, invokes stored closures, completes the frame and clears the replay flag. Limitations: The replay flag is state, not a lock. Polling it is not sufficient to synchronize a write.
Actual timing-thread entry invokes1287D0 then _endthreadex. Limitations: This disproves an assumption that presentation always shares the engine update thread.
Actual application-thread entry invokes121D90, then the managed-close bridge and _endthreadex. Limitations: The managed callback and process-wide exit flow are outside this narrow control contract.

The application loop calls app virtual Update at slot+32, repeats on0, invokes draw on1 and otherwise enters shutdown. Limitations: Reject trainer actions when the original Update requested shutdown; do not assume the current host thread is the application thread.

Renderer startup stores App at GX+1000, creates device/root signature/shaders, sets brightness0 and gamma1, then creates application thread handle+784 and timing-thread handle+792. Renderer destruction destroys GX+30848 mutex and PSO/command/resource containers before changing the final base vtable and releasing device+736. Limitations: Vtable/device checks alone can remain positive partway through destruction; application-thread/exit/lifecycle gates are necessary.

Limitations: Static xrefs identify a CLR-exported native method; the exact managed caller is separate evidence. Do not call this shutdown API from the trainer.

Creates a submission marker node with two links and a 16-byte payload: QPC timestamp, submission ordinal and backbuffer index. Limitations: This is a point event; it does not measure a duration or count primitive draw calls.

Creates a Present timeline node with a 32-byte payload after its two link pointers. Limitations: Only the initialized begin/end ticks and three DWORD fields are meaningful; padding is not a diagnostic value.

Copies a 56-byte timing-worker cycle record into a linked-list node, including six QPC timestamps and a state DWORD. Limitations: Several optional-phase timestamps are conditional; no general-purpose timing plot should assume every timestamp is refreshed on every cycle.
Creates a wait timeline node with a 24-byte payload after two links: QPC begin/end and a native wait category. Limitations: The final four bytes are padding, not an extra wait field.

Limitations: The recorded interval includes any elapsed wall-clock time between the boundaries; it is not exclusive CPU execution time.

Brackets the actual swapchain Present1 call with QPC ticks and records it in list+944 (cap30); stores requested interval and actual/prior backbuffer indices. The real Present interval can be0 despite a nonzero recorded request. Limitations: CPU time inside Present is not GPU frame time, display latency or monitor scanout duration.

Appends a24-byte fence/wait record under the supplied critical section, removes the tail at count200, inserts at the head and releases the lock. Limitations: It copies caller-supplied data; timestamp/category semantics come from the three concrete callers.

Waits for a completed native fence, logs its CPU wait, maps completed command-buffer query pairs, converts GPU timestamps through per-buffer GPU/CPU calibration and frequency into CPU QPC units, appends GPU records (cap300), and feeds the adaptive quality history. Limitations: Fresh ASM uses signed64-bit subtraction/conversion and float32 arithmetic; misleading DWORD casts in pseudocode are not the ABI. Each list record is a command-buffer span, not automatically a full frame.

Signals/increments a fence packet, waits when necessary, and appends a category0 CPU wait record to list+912. Limitations: This function performs real GPU synchronization and must never be called merely to refresh diagnostics.
Shifts a fixed64-float history toward older indices and writes its XMM1 sample to index0. Limitations: Only caller129180 establishes that the sample is GPU time normalized by59.94/QPC-frequency.

Evaluates the64-sample GPU cost history and a frame-period budget. Low headroom can lower AA quality by two levels; sustained high headroom across30 samples can raise it by one; results are bounded by caller limits. It resets history/counters on adjustment. Limitations: This is adaptive AA policy, not a generic FPS limiter. The XMM2 floating argument is explicit in caller ASM, although the decompiler inferred an integer at the call site.

Consumes resize requests under resize CS+31432; rebuilds resources after a fence wait when needed. Limitations: The AMD/vendor flag limits the adaptive exponent to0 on this path. Directly freezing30556 would bypass native resource and replay coordination.

Takes GX inRCX, targetID inEDX and sample exponent inR8B; writes target sample count1<<exponent and recreates existing color/depth resources via11B4F0/11B290 when the count changes. Begins a recording interval by clearing per-interval state, capturing QPC start at GX+976 and replay flag at+992; normal frames run resize/adaptive policy, while replay restores historical AA levels. Limitations: A coherent snapshot may still legitimately describe a replayed sample configuration; quality level and displayed frame identity are not interchangeable.

Finishes the native presentation pass, submits command lists, consumes completed GPU timing, rotates frame/context indices, presents, then runs GC on all three framebuffer resource managers. Limitations: Its synchronization and command submission make it unsuitable for a trainer-triggered refresh.

Acquires GX presentation mutex+30848 around close/flush/present, deferred release-ring collection, next recording-interval setup and DummyDraw enqueue; unlocks before the final application call. Limitations: This proves the native lock order presentation mutex then history CS for snapshots that need both.

Native FVECTOR2 constructor consists only of mov rax,rcx and ret. It does not initialize either component. The BaseSimpleForm constructor calls it for32 stack entries before querying resolutions. Resolution wrapper preserves the caller buffer/count/aspect-filter, obtains the GX singleton through11C150, and dispatches11C970. Resolution enumeration copies at most the caller's capacity and normally returns the number written. If zero entries were written, it recursively calls itself with aspect filtering disabled, discards the recursive return count and forces return1. The fallback has no separate guard when filtering was already disabled, so no eligible mode (or zero capacity with eligible modes) can follow an unbounded recursive path. Returned1 does not establish that exactly one vector was written. Limitations: Observed machine-code path only. No runtime reproduction, display-mode manipulation or inferred frequency. Eligible native modes are >=800x600 and optionally exact16:9.

Publishes the nested pref BAR and first type2 plyr/fmab/prty/magi/sstm payloads. The signed DWORD at sstm payload+4 is added to that payload to install system parameters, or produces null when zero. Loads the system BAR, publishes it at RVA2AE5E50 and passes its first type2 pref payload to3E9360. Developer setup passes float4 to the scale setter, then separately overrides retention to 4*system parameter+76 +500. This differs from the ordinary setter's scaled parameter+80. Script trap reads a float argument and tail-calls the target-search-scale setter with XMM0. Limitations: Static behavior in the exact Steam1.0.0.2 executable. Resource contents, target exceptions and live engine interactions are not validated by synthetic tests.

Manual acquisition iterates eligible actors and type3 target points. Uses global scale*system parameter+76, skips point bit1, applies distance minus target-point radius and ranks candidates by proximity. Resource contents, target exceptions and live engine interactions are not validated by synthetic tests.

Automatic selector uses player parameter+92 for radius, +96/+100 for vertical bounds, and +108/+112 for vertical/facing score. Limitations: Static behavior in the exact Steam1.0.0.2 executable. Resource contents, target exceptions and live engine interactions are not validated by synthetic tests.

Manual target cycling excludes the current actor/point and orders candidates by signed angular direction. XMM3 supplies the direction omitted by some decompiler signatures. Resource contents, target exceptions and live engine interactions are not validated by synthetic tests.

Normal targeting update validates scene/input/actor conditions and current target.
